incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: realtime.slo.generate-text (us-east-1) triggered at 2026-03-15T09:12:12Z — p95=780ms (SLO 500ms), p99=3120ms (SLO 1500ms). Grafana: /d/realtime/latency?panel=generate-text. Rule: realtime-latency-regression. Pager: ops-oncall.

Avery (oncall): Acked — I'm paged and looking. Anyone on the realtime path able to join?

Maria (SRE): I'm on. quick gut checks: grafana shows p95 jump starting ~09:10, QPS steady, error rate normal. Streaming completion latency panel shows many long tails on worker group rt-stream-1.

Devon (runtime): saw that too. The streaming workers show elevated loop times on KV lookup stage. KV cache miss ratio jumped from 2% -> 48% for recent windows. Could be KVCACHE invalidation or a bad rollout.

Avery (oncall): Was there any recent deploy around 02:30 UTC?

Devon (runtime): Yeah, rolled out kv-cache ttl change and a small cache sharding tweak at 02:28 (deploy id: deploy-2026-03-15-028). No errors reported during deploy smoke.

Ashley (prod-eng): If kv miss ratio is high, streaming stalls are expected — each miss triggers backend fetch + longer KV serialization. Two quick mitigations: 1) temporarily bypass KV caching for realtime route, 2) route streaming requests to standby pool with older runtime. Which is faster?

Maria (SRE): Bypass cache sounds lower blast radius. We can flip feature flag for generate-text to skip kv-cache on streaming paths. I can patch the flag now.

Avery (oncall): Go ahead Maria. Also spin up 3 extra rt-stream workers in us-east to buy time. Devon, can you run scale?

Devon (runtime): On it. Running:

```bash
# scale realtime streaming pool
rctl scale pool rt-stream-1 --add 3 --region us-east-1
```

Devon (runtime): Command accepted, new replicas requested. kube events show pods coming up.

Maria (SRE): Flipping flag: `feature.realtime.kv_bypass = true` for service=generate-text (canary->all). Pushing patch...

Maria (SRE): Patch applied. Re-evaluating metrics — p95 dropping to ~420ms within 40s, p99 falling to ~1100ms.

Avery (oncall): Nice. Keep an eye for regressions. Any customer-facing impact we should flag? Kat from support, can you check active customers with heavy streaming usage?

Kat (support): Looking. Two large customers (AcmeAI, NimbusHealth) have elevated session latencies reported via monitoring. No error spikes and no dropped sessions — just slower streaming responses. I'll open proactive support tickets and pasteie a short note to customers: "We're mitigating a streaming latency issue; temporary fix applied; performance should improve within minutes; engineering investigating root cause."

Ashley (prod-eng): Good. Also create an incident in the tracker and capture the deploy id + KV config change. I'm logging INC-2026-045 with initial severity P2 (customer impact limited but SLO breached). Link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2026-045

Avery (oncall): Action log so far:
- 09:12 alert fired (thread 5098765432)
- 09:13 paged oncall (Avery)
- 09:14 scale rt-stream-1 +3 (Devon)
- 09:15 set feature.realtime.kv_bypass=true (Maria)
- 09:16 metrics improved (p95 < SLO)
- Incident created INC-2026-045 (Ashley)

Devon (runtime): I'm capturing a few flame graphs and traces from traced requests where KV miss occurred. Example trace snippet for request id r-0a1b2c3d:

```
span: request r-0a1b2c3d
  - recv -> 1ms
  - kv_lookup (miss) -> 380ms
  - backend_fetch -> 220ms
  - serialization -> 60ms
  - stream_send -> 5ms
```

Devon (runtime): These KV misses are expensive — miss path includes a blocking fetch to model-cache store. We'll want to rollback the sharding change in the next window if we confirm correlation.

Maria (SRE): Agreed. For now, keep kv_bypass=true until we can validate rollback. I'll add a watch rule for kv_miss_ratio > 25% to page during recovery window.

Kat (support): I've notified account managers for AcmeAI and NimbusHealth and set expectation: "intermittent high streaming latency; mitigation applied; ongoing investigation; next update in 30m".

Avery (oncall): Handoff plan: I'm staying on for the next 20 minutes to confirm stability; if p95 holds under SLO, I'll assign follow-up to Devon/Ashley for root-cause and rollback plan. Who will lead RCA?

Ashley (prod-eng): Devon + Maria will run RCA. I'll coordinate release and rollback timeline with runtime infra.

Devon (runtime): Will start a focused bisect of the deploy (deploy-2026-03-15-028) and run a canary rollback in a staging subset. Prefetching results and will post findings here.

Maria (SRE): Current metrics: p95=380ms, p99=940ms, kv_miss_ratio down to 4% after bypass + extra pods. Looks stable for now.

Avery (oncall): Good work. Please keep incident status up-to-date in INC-2026-045. I'll close the on-call page once ASHLEY confirms assignment for RCA and rollback.

incident-bot: Note: Ops page will auto-close after 2h of no further pages.

Kat (support): I'll post an update to customers in 30 minutes and close the urgent account threads if numbers continue to improve.

Devon (runtime): Quick note — recording the diagnostic commands used (for postmortem):

```bash
# trace samples
traces fetch --service rt-stream-1 --from 2026-03-15T09:08 --to 2026-03-15T09:18 --filter "kv_lookup>100ms"

# check kv metrics
promql 'sum(rate(kv_lookup_miss_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_lookup_total[5m]))'
```

Avery (oncall): Thanks everyone. Leaving the thread open for RCA updates. If anything regresses, re-page ops-oncall. :thumbsup: :eyes:
